summary: POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a Bridgepoint Health pilot. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, correctness), workload sizing, benchmark plan, timelines, and required infosec artifacts (SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs). Agreed next steps to exchange security docs, run benchmarks, and set up SAML test tenant.
topics: POC success criteria (latency p95, throughput, accuracy)
Workload sizing (daily tokens, seq length, concurrency)
Security & compliance: SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS
transcript: Meeting header: 2028-04-11 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 mins | Attendees: Katrina, Samir (Redwood); Maya, Jorge, Lina, Avery (Bridgepoint)
[00:00] Katrina: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, quick agenda — scope success criteria, sizing, security reqs for the pilot, and next steps

[00:12] Maya: thanks Katrina, yeah from our side Jorge and I are leading security, Lina is ML lead, Avery is infra. We're thinking a 6-week pilot focused on PII-safe summarization of patient intake notes

[00:28] Jorge: quick note — we need SOC 2 or ISO evidence, plus SSO via SAML, RBAC, and audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance. Retention is 7 years for certain logs, that's non-negotiable for audits

[00:42] Katrina: totally understood, we can provide our SOC 2 report and ISO 27001 cert, and we support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. For logs we can forward to Splunk or provide S3 exports — Samir, want to add on the infra side?

[00:58] Samir: yeah, and to be clear, we have Hosted and Dedicated options. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools, configurable autoscaling, and direct VPC peering for log drain. Hosted can be configured with long-term log retention via our add-on but default is shorter. There may be tradeoffs vs cost

[01:18] Lina: for the ML bits, we care about latency p95 under 300ms for single-turn prompts | and throughput of roughly 50 concurrent requests at peak. Daily token volume estimate: around 2M tokens, average seq length ~512 but some longer at 1k tokens occasionally
[01:40] Avery: infra question — will Redwood support KMS/HSM integration? We need customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption

[01:52] Katrina: yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for Private customers. For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account roles and for Private deployments you retain full key control

[02:10] Jorge: and audit logs — we need immutable logs with user-level attribution, ideally with connections to our SSO (SAML) so we can map actions back to users. Also, RBAC must let us separate dev/test/admin roles

[02:30] Samir: our Console exposes token-level cost and per-route tracing, and audit logs include admin actions, model deployments, and API key usage. There's occasional noise in the auto-transcripts — but we capture event IDs for correlation
[03:00] Maya: success criteria wise — what would you propose we measure during the pilot?

[03:08] Katrina: recommend three success buckets: 1) Security/compliance: you have the docs, SAML setup, RBAC matrix, and logs integrated; 2) Performance: meet latency p95 target and throughput targets for peak windows; 3) Quality: model outputs meet accuracy thresholds on your eval set (we'll use a small labeled prompt set for regression checks)
[03:30] Lina: for quality, we can provide a prompt set of ~200 labeled examples. We'll want automatic regression alerts if output quality drops beyond 5% vs baseline

[03:45] Samir: good — we'll wire up Redwood Optimize to run continuous evals against that prompt set and surface regressions. For benchmarking we'll run both Hosted and Dedicated variants with the same workload and compare latency/cost
[04:05] Jorge: how do you handle data retention and deletion requests? For ePHI we need to ensure we can purge data on demand

[04:12] Katrina: we support customer data deletion per API and also offer configurable data retention policies. For Private you control the retention; for Hosted we have controls and can work with legal for a DPA clause about ePHI. We'll include that in the security packet
[04:30] Avery: what's the timeline for the pilot? We're aiming for production decision in 8 weeks from now

[04:36] Katrina: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks plus a 2-week bake period for integration. Proposed: Week 1 (onboarding, share docs), Week 2 (SAML + RBAC + log integration), Week 3-4 (benchmark runs), Week 5 (analysis + fixes), Week 6 (decision meeting). We can compress if you have resources
[05:00] Maya: that aligns. Can you share an explicit benchmark plan — metrics, scripts, and cost model?

[05:06] Samir: yes — plan will include synthetic load with your token distribution, p95/p99 latency, tail-kv cache hit rates, throughput at target concurrency, and cost per 1k tokens after batching and caching. We'll include runbooks and scripts
[05:30] Lina: on the performance note — caching is important. Some patient-intake forms reuse prefixes; how does Redwood handle KV cache and prefix caching?

[05:40] Samir: automatic prefix and KV caching is supported for compatible models; we also expose cache hit metrics so you can tune prompt design. There's also quantization options to reduce inference cost if you care about slight quality/cost tradeoffs
[06:05] Jorge: about RBAC — we need an admin role, security-reader, developer, and SRE roles. Can you map those to SAML groups?
[06:15] Katrina: yes, we map SAML group attributes to Console roles and you can customize permissions per-route and per-model. We'll send a sample RBAC matrix
[06:30] Avery: Splunk forwarding — is it via syslog, or do you push to S3? We want near real-time ingestion

[06:38] Samir: we can forward events over an authenticated syslog endpoint, or ship to S3 with a Lambda to forward; for Dedicated we can offer VPC egress to your SIEM with <1min lag. We'll note the options in the security packet
[06:55] Maya: any blockers on our side for SAML? We use Okta and can provide metadata
[07:02] Katrina: Okta is standard, we'll exchange metadata and set up a test tenant; we'll also include instructions for SAML attribute mappings
[07:15] Jorge: data residency — some PHI needs to stay in us-east-1. Can Redwood pin region for the pilot?
[07:22] Samir: yes we can pin host region for Dedicated and Hosted in supported regions; for Private deployments you of course choose on-prem or a specific region

[07:35] Lina: benchmark specifics: we'll want to run 3 runs at low/med/high concurrency and capture p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and cost. Also measure model quality metrics like Rouge or BLEU for summarization
[07:55] Samir: understood. We'll add a QA harness to compute those metrics against your eval set. We'll include model variant recommendations and quantization profiles that match your quality bar
[08:10] Maya: what about fallback policies — if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, can you route to hosted compatible variants? We need graceful degradation
[08:18] Katrina: yes, smart routing can failover to a compatible model variant and we can set policies by latency or cost. We'll document expected latencies in the runbook
[08:35] Jorge: please also include an audit trail of who triggered fallbacks and model rollouts, that needs to be in the logs
[08:42] Samir: audit entries for rollout actions are included with user IDs and timestamps, we also keep deployment diffs in the console audit
[09:00] (brief cross talk)

[09:15] Katrina: ok recap — security: we'll send SOC2 + ISO, SAML integration guide, RBAC matrix, log forwarding options; infra: benchmark plan and scripts; sample eval set from Bridgepoint; timeline proposed. Does that look right?
[09:30] Maya: yes, looks good. One question — are there any penetration test options? We may want a pen test kickoff
[09:38] Katrina: we offer third-party penetration test reports for Dedicated and Private customers; for Hosted we'll provide summary results and can coordinate a joint test engagement if needed
[09:50] Jorge: also need to confirm data-in-transit encryption between Redwood and our VPC endpoints
[09:55] Samir: TLS everywhere, and for Dedicated we can peer VPCs for private traffic; we'll include the network diagram in the packet
[10:10] Lina: small note — sometimes auto-transcripts change product names, e.g., Redwood Dedicated -> 'red wood dedicated' in transcripts, so please ignore that in docs
[10:22] Katrina: haha noted, our transcripts are not perfect :)
[10:30] Maya: timeline acceptance — we'll try to get the sample workload and Okta metadata by Friday 2028-04-14
[10:36] Avery: I'll own sample traffic and SIEM endpoints
[10:40] Jorge: I'll confirm retention policy and compliance checklist
[10:45] Katrina: perfect, we'll turn around the security packet and benchmark plan. Any final concerns?
[10:53] Maya: curious about cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted at our scale — we'll need that in the cost model
[10:58] Samir: we'll include a per-token and per-hour breakdown factoring in batching and cache hit assumptions. We'll present three scenarios: conservative, expected, optimistic
[11:18] (wrap up)
[11:25] Katrina: thanks everyone, next steps are in the follow-up, we'll send the packet and propose times for the benchmark run
[11:33] Maya: thanks Katrina, bye
[11:35] Meeting end
